title: feat(ants): Add ANTs as a registration backend
body:
#### Overview

This PR introduces ANTs (Advanced Normalization Tools) as a new, fully integrated registration backend for `brainreg`. This provides users with a powerful, widely-used alternative to the existing NiftyReg backend, leveraging the high-level `antspyx` Python library for a clean and robust implementation.

The integration is designed to be seamless, allowing users to switch backends with a single `--backend ants` command-line flag. The core `brainreg` pipeline remains backend-agnostic, with all ANTs-specific logic cleanly encapsulated within its own module.

---

#### Key Architectural Changes

-   **Modular Backend Structure:** A new `brainreg/core/backend/ants/` directory has been created, mirroring the existing `niftyreg` structure. This ensures a clean separation of concerns and makes the codebase easy to navigate and maintain.
-   **High-Level Abstraction:** Instead of calling external binaries, this backend interfaces directly with the `antspyx` library. This simplifies command execution, error handling, and dependency management.
-   **Configuration-driven:** User-facing ANTs parameters are exposed via a dedicated `ants_parse` group in the CLI, allowing for fine-tuned control over the registration process (e.g., `--ants-transform-type`).

#### Feature Implementation

-   [x] **CLI Integration:** The `--backend` option now includes `ants`, and a new argument group for ANTs-specific settings is available.
-   [x] **Core Pipeline Integration:** The main `brainreg` orchestrator now dynamically dispatches to the correct `run_*` function based on the selected backend.
-   [x] **Complete Workflow:** The `run_ants` function handles the full end-to-end process:
    -   Preparation of `ANTsImage` objects from NumPy arrays.
    -   Execution of `ants.registration()` using user-defined parameters.
    -   Application of forward transforms to warp atlas annotations and hemispheres (`genericLabel` interpolation is used for accuracy).
    -   Application of inverse transforms to warp the sample brain and any additional channels to standard space.
    -   Extraction and saving of the 3D deformation field components.
-   [x] **Feature Parity:** All major `brainreg` features are supported, including `additional_images_downsample` and `save_original_orientation`.
-   [x] **Robust Cleanup:** Intermediate files are stored in a temporary `ants/` subdirectory and are automatically removed unless `--debug` is specified.
- #### Housekeeping
-   **CI Fix:** The `ruff` pre-commit hook was failing due to a deprecated `fix = true` key in `pyproject.toml`. I have removed this key to align with modern Ruff configuration and ensure CI passes for this PR.

#### How to Test

1.  Ensure `antspyx` is installed in the environment (`pip install antspyx`).
2.  Run a standard registration using the new backend. The `SyN` transform is fast and suitable for testing:
    ```bash
    brainreg /path/to/sample/data /path/to/output -v 5 2 2 --orientation psl --backend ants --ants-transform-type SyN
    ```
3.  Verify that the output directory contains the expected final files (`registered_atlas.tiff`, `volumes.csv`, etc.) and that the registration quality is reasonable upon inspection in Napari.
4.  Run a regression test using the default NiftyReg backend to ensure no existing functionality has been broken:
    ```bash
    brainreg /path/to/sample/data /path/to/output_niftyreg -v 5 2 2 --orientation psl --backend niftyreg
    ```

This contribution enhances the flexibility and power of `brainreg` by incorporating one of the most respected toolkits in the neuroimaging community. Looking forward to your feedback.

title: [BUG] The GUI does not allow negative values in key parameter boxes
body:
**Describe the bug**
The default parameters in the Graphical User Interface (GUI) do not match with those in the Command Line Interface (CLI), resulting in inconsistent alignment outcomes depending on whether alignment is computed through the GUI or CLI.

Based on the documentation negative values set the units in pixels while positive values set values in millimeters (mm). 
https://brainglobe.info/documentation/brainreg/user-guide/parameters.html

The real issue is that the GUI only accepts positive values for parameters like **grid_spacing**, **smoothing_sigma_reference**, and **smoothing_sigma_floating**, making it impossible to input negative values.

**To Reproduce**
Compute any alignment in CLI and GUI and then compare the outcomes. 

**Expected behaviour**
Same outcomes regardless the use of CLI or GUI.

**Log file**
[brainreg_2024-04-26_09-49-50_CLI.log](https://github.com/brainglobe/brainreg/files/15160577/brainreg_2024-04-26_09-49-50_CLI.log)
[brainreg_2024-04-26_10-16-26_GUI.log](https://github.com/brainglobe/brainreg/files/15160578/brainreg_2024-04-26_10-16-26_GUI.log)

Key parameters when using CLI:
- grid_spacing: -10
- smoothing_sigma_reference: -1.0
- smoothing_sigma_floating: -1.0

Key parameters when using GUI:
- grid_spacing: 10
- smoothing_sigma_reference: 1
- smoothing_sigma_floating: 1.0

**Screenshots**
Alignment when using CLI
![image](https://github.com/brainglobe/brainreg/assets/64906929/bdf5ec8a-f85a-407f-b19c-dd9bf5af45cf)
Alignment when using GUI
![image](https://github.com/brainglobe/brainreg/assets/64906929/8948bc48-53f2-4578-b620-0f1ea65b3fde)

**Conclusion**
The GUI does not allow negative values in the parameter boxes for grid_spacing, smoothing_sigma_reference, and smoothing_sigma_floating.

This uses the same `QScrollArea` solution as the `cellfinder` [detect](https://github.com/brainglobe/cellfinder/blob/main/cellfinder/napari/detect/detect.py#L229) and [train](https://github.com/brainglobe/cellfinder/blob/main/cellfinder/napari/train/train.py#L180) widgets. A better solution would be to change all widgets to use `qtpy` directly, but this isn't a very quick fix.
